brief: A cabinet of three cells with two drawers, one of them shown pulled open.

requirements.evidence: Three full hex bases in a straight line at axial (-1,0), (0,0), (1,0) level 0 (piece refs piece:-1,0,0;full, piece:0,0,0;full, piece:1,0,0;full), closed with solid end caps and joint bolts; check_build reports no issues and meshClash clear.

Two notch drawers (notch:0#0,1#notch1 with hex-drawer-frame-notch-fm, and notch:0#0,-1#notch4 with hex-drawer-frame-notch-mf) sit in the empty spots beside the touching bases. They are notch drawers, not drawers set into the cells: cell drawers on the half-base cut faces were refused from pulling out because the neighbouring base blocked them.
The notch drawer at (0,1) is set open (setNotchOpen k=1). The other drawer at (0,-1) is closed. Pulling the drawer open is accepted by the configurator with no overlap.

finish.summary: Built a three-cell cabinet: three full bases in a row, with two notch drawers in the empty spots beside the touching cells, one open. Caps and joint bolts are added per house rules and check_build is clean with mesh clear. Caveat: I first tried slide drawers built into the end half-cells, but they could not be pulled out because the centre cell blocked them, so I used notch drawers instead. The drawers sit beside the cabinet rather than inside its cells.

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
